stem.en: Two sisters have the same parents, yet they look different. What is the best reason?

text.en: Each got a different mix of chromosomes.

feedback.en: Yes. Each gamete carries its own mix, so each child is a new combination.

text.en: One sister got more chromosomes than the other.

feedback.en: Both have 46 chromosomes. The mix differs, not the number.

text.en: Only the older sister got chromosomes from both.

feedback.en: Every child gets chromosomes from both parents.

text.en: Their cells were made by different kinds of mitosis.

feedback.en: Meiosis makes the gametes, and that is where the mixing happens.

explanation.en: In meiosis each pair sorts by chance, so each gamete carries its own mix. Two sisters come from different gametes, so they differ.

hints.en: Do the sisters have different numbers of chromosomes?
